overview: MQ-series sensors detect gases using a heated tin-dioxide element whose electrical resistance changes when specific gases pass over it — the MQ-2 is tuned for combustible gas/smoke (LPG, methane, smoke), while the MQ-135 targets general air quality gases (CO2, ammonia, benzene, and other pollutants). Both share the same core gotcha: the heating element needs a warm-up ('burn-in') period — anywhere from a couple of minutes to 24-48 hours for a brand-new sensor — before readings stabilize, and the raw analog output is a relative resistance change, not a calibrated gas concentration, so getting an actual PPM figure requires per-sensor calibration against the datasheet's response curves.
simpleSummary: A sensor that detects gases like smoke or CO2 in the air.

specifications.warmupTime: Minutes (basic stabilization) up to 24-48 hours (full sensor burn-in for new units)
specifications.outputType: Analog (resistance-based, proportional to gas concentration) and digital (threshold, trimpot-adjustable)
specifications.targetGasesMQ135: CO2, ammonia (NH3), benzene, alcohol, general air quality

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.function: Power input, also feeds the internal heating element.
pinMap.gotcha: The heater draws meaningfully more current than most beginner sensors — don't power multiple gas sensors directly from a microcontroller's 5V pin.

pinMap.name: AOUT
pinMap.function: Analog output proportional to gas concentration (as a resistance-ratio signal, not a calibrated PPM value).
pinMap.gotcha: Don't trust the raw voltage as an absolute PPM reading without calibrating against the sensor's datasheet curve for the specific gas of interest.

pinMap.name: DOUT
pinMap.function: Digital threshold output, adjustable via the onboard trimpot.

useCases.title: Gas leak / smoke alarm
useCases.scenario: MQ-2 configured to trigger an alert when combustible gas or smoke crosses a threshold.

useCases.title: Indoor air quality monitor
useCases.scenario: MQ-135 tracking general air quality trends for a smart-home dashboard.

useCases.title: Ventilation automation
useCases.scenario: Automatically switch on a fan or vent when air quality readings degrade.

oftenConfusedWith: Flame sensors (detect fire's IR signature, not gas composition)
oftenUpgradedTo: Calibrated digital air-quality sensors (e.g. CCS811, SGP30) for actual PPM-accurate readings
